details:
LunarBase: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a 3D interactive educational game where players become the commander of a lunar base. Their goal is to keep the astronaut crew alive during a five-day simulated Moon mission.

Players must manage important resources such as oxygen, water, food, and power. During the mission, they face different challenges, including radiation alerts and equipment failures. They must make decisions, manage limited resources, and protect their crew. Their decisions affect the mission's progress and the survival of the astronauts.

The game uses NASA's open data resources to support its scientific content. NASA DONKI provides real space-weather event data, while NASA OSDR RadLab provides radiation measurement data from spaceflight research. These resources help us introduce real space science concepts into the game. The lunar mission scenarios and gameplay consequences are simulations created for educational purposes, not real-time predictions of lunar conditions.

The main benefit of LunarBase is that it makes learning about space exploration more interactive. Instead of only reading about the challenges of living on the Moon, players experience them through decision-making and gameplay. It can help young learners understand the importance of resource management, radiation protection, problem-solving, and teamwork during future space missions.

We developed the project as a 3D browser-based game using Google AI Studio's Build mode and AI-assisted development. We used NASA's publicly available data resources, including DONKI and OSDR RadLab, to support the scientific information presented in the game. No special hardware is required to play it.

The creative part of our project is combining space science with a survival and resource-management game. We wanted to make the experience educational but also enjoyable and challenging. While developing it, we considered the needs of young learners, simple controls, understandable instructions, limited resources, different mission challenges, and the importance of presenting scientific information responsibly.

Our intended impact is to inspire young learners to explore space science and better understand the challenges astronauts may face when humans establish bases on the Moon.
